title: What a strings allowlist entry turns off, and what the share counts
body:
**Chose:** a `strings` entry stops every rule from reading strings in its files (`id-string`, and the string half of `line-cite` and `section-cite`); comments, names and paths there still hit. Files under an `all` entry are left out of the comment share too. An allow entry with a key other than `path` or `scope` is an error, like an unknown scope.
**Over:** turning off only the `id-string` row; counting `all` files in the share; ignoring unknown keys.
**Because:** the PRD calls the scope "the string check", and allowlisted files hold recorded tool output (`src/x.rs:3` lines, section cites) as data. Recorded fixtures under `all` are thousands of comment-free lines that would dilute the figure. A typo like `scop = "all"` would silently fall back to `strings`.
**Undo:** `scope_of` and the `strings` flag in `leaks::check`; the key check in `leaks::allowlist`.

title: The extension table and comment split beyond the PRD's list
body:
**Chose:** the js family also covers mjs, cjs, jsx, tsx, mts and cts; sh covers bash; yaml covers yml. A leading `*` makes a comment line only as `*`, `* …` or `*/`, so a Rust deref like `*count += 1` stays code. `#` starts a comment only at the line start or after a space, and `#[` in PHP is an attribute. Rust char literals, lifetimes and raw strings are parsed so a `'"'` or `r#"…"#` does not open a false string.
**Over:** the PRD's bare list and a leading `*` of any kind.
**Because:** factory's own tree has `docs.mjs`, and every false string swallows the comment behind it.
**Undo:** `leaks::syntax` and `leaks::split`.

title: Drop "no longer" from the history row
body:
**Chose:** drop "no longer" from the `history` row's word list.
**Over:** keeping it and accepting the false hits; a narrower "no longer" pattern.
**Because:** over cody and arca, about 45 of its 110 comment hits describe a present state ("a row that is no longer pending", "Agent no longer exists", "node the spec no longer has"). The history uses ("The funnel no longer calls…") take the same verb shapes, so no detector tells them apart. The slice's acceptance is no false hit. The cost: a real "no longer" history comment now passes, and polish's reader question is what still covers it.
**Undo:** add `no longer` back to the `history` pattern in `src/leaks.rs` and drop the `no longer pending` non-hit in its `history` test.

title: Which senses of used to, previously and for now are not history
body:
**Chose:** blank three non-history senses out of a comment before the `history` row runs: "used to" as purpose (after `,;:(—–-`, after a form of be or get, a modal, never or not, or after rules, path, key, mapping, field, column, header, token or helper), "previously" as an adjective (after a determiner, or `previously <verb>ed <noun>s`), and "for now and".
**Over:** a per-repo rule table (the PRD rules it out); keeping the false hits.
**Because:** cody and arca hold about 60 of these ("the key used to sign", "Get the validation rules used to validate", "a previously accepted memory", "returns YYYYMM for now and the following month"). The cost: a history comment in those exact shapes ("the flag was used to gate X") passes.
**Undo:** the three `history` entries of `QUIET` in `src/leaks.rs` and the `purpose` cases in its `history` test.

title: Foreign names the id and finding rows skip
body:
**Chose:** five more shapes are not hits: a one-digit `L` (`L7` network layer; two-digit `L11` still hits), `S3` (the storage service), a `§` right after `RFC <n>` or `manual` (`RFC 7636 §4.2`, `WSAA manual §10.6`), an id followed by a package version (`slice-1.0.4.tgz`, `block-3.31.3`; `FR-1.2` still hits), `cp` with three or more digits (`cp1252`), and a whole `slice<n>` identifier in a `.go` file (`slice2Allowlists` still hits).
**Over:** keeping them as hits; allowlisting the files.
**Because:** each one fired on cody or arca on a foreign name, not a plan id. The cost: a finding called `L2`…`L9` or `S3`, and a Go variable named after a slice, now pass.
**Undo:** the `finding-id` pattern, the `id-comment` and `SEMVER` entries of `QUIET`, the `cp` digit check in `name_hit`, and `go_slice`, all in `src/leaks.rs`.

title: The lane's cargo target dir is target/lane-1
body: The lane builds into target/lane-1 (CARGO_TARGET_DIR), so the binary is target/lane-1/debug/factory, not target/debug/factory.

title: What an allowlist path may hold, and the exit code when the scan cannot run
body:
**Chose:** an allowlist `path` is a file or folder relative to the repo root. A leading `./` is trimmed; an empty path, an absolute path, or one holding `*`, `?` or `[` is an error naming the entry. `factory leaks` exits 2 when the scan cannot run, 1 only on hits.
**Over:** taking the path literally (it then covers nothing, silently); reading globs; one exit code for both hits and failure.
**Because:** the PRD names paths, not patterns, and a glob that silently matches nothing leaves the hits in place with no hint why. Exit 2 is what the polish skill already reads as "did not run".
**Undo:** the path check in `leaks::allowlist`; the `Ok(2)` arm in `src/cli/leaks.rs`.

title: AD-4 changed
body: Flag them all: "used to" as purpose, "previously" as an adjective and "for now and" are history hits again. The three `history` entries of `QUIET` in `src/leaks.rs` go, and the purpose cases in its `history` test assert hits. The owner takes the ~60 false hits on cody and arca over a history comment in those shapes passing.
